en:
"Oh, so you finally solved the Beldoll!?
Then let us apply the finishing touch!"{w}
note: editorial: 'the Beldoll' for the item, as in slices 022/028.

en: Bilente took out a key made of the same material as the Beldoll and threaded all of the Beldoll's separated rings onto it.{w}
note: editorial: 'the Beldoll' for the item, as in slices 022/028.

en: "Now then, Beldoll.{w}Lay bare the wonders that dwell within you, here before my eyes... Nnfuh!"{w}
Smoke rose from the puzzle ring, and a violent shock struck you!{w}And then...{w}
"Hah hah hah!{w}Somebody who can solve me finally showed up!!"{w}
"Hm? And who exactly are you...?"{w}
Before you stood a small demon.{w}Its bizarre figure brought a jester to mind.{w}
note: "Its" for the demon (a creature, gender unstated); avoids he/she.

en: Beldoll

"I'm Beldoll, the Demon of Wisdom!
Nice to meetcha!!"{w}
note: Glossary position: 'Demon of Wisdom'. Beldoll's ore-cchi = cocky slangy voice.

en: "Forgive me for rushing you, but...{w}might I humbly ask you to show me your very best wonder, just once...?"{w}

"My very best wonder?{w}I came out of a puzzle ring, didn't I?
That's wonder enough! Wahahahaa!"{w}
"What's wrong? Go ahead, be amazed."{w}
"Surely... you don't mean I'm supposed to be amazed just because you came out?"{w}
"Well, obviously?"{w}
note: Source mochiron with a question mark: a puzzled 'of course?'.

en: "...Haaaaaahhh~~~!!"{w}
note: A long, deflated sigh (Beldoll calls it a sigh next row).

en: "Huh? What's with that sigh!?"{w}
"At this stage, of all things! Of all things, the whole act is just the entrance!!{w}After all the trouble you put me and these adventurers through, this is the extent of your wonder?"{w}
note: de-ochi = a joke that is spent the moment the performer appears; rendered descriptively. | editorial: de-ochi made clear (the entrance is the whole act); avoids the doubled 'After all' opening.
{11:...} is a runtime spell-name insert (same code family used for spells elsewhere); kept verbatim, chanted with ~ as in the source.

en:
"Honestly,
you've disappointed me, my dear Beldoll."{w}{p}"A demon popping out of an object, granting wishes...{w}Just look around this shop.{w}These shelves are overflowing with junk like that."{w}
note: Beldoll-san = 'my dear Beldoll' (polite-sardonic; avoids Mr./Ms.). | editorial: kusaru hodo = more than plenty; 'rotting with' read as literal decay.

en: "No wayyy!?"{w}
"No, this won't do. All that, and nothing to show for it!{w}Come now, show me a wonder worthy of my expense and my expectations."{w}
note: editorial: mukuwarenai = the trouble/expense goes unrewarded; old wording was vague.

en: "Hngh..."{w}
"Show me a wonder, won't you...{w}my dear Beldoll... Heh heh?"{w}
note: editorial: Bilente's fufu = 'Heh heh' capitalised as in slice 022.

en: Wearing a brazen grin, Bilente inched closer to Beldoll.{w}
note: Source writes [JP] (typo for [JP] 'fearless/brazen').

en: "Y-yeek!?"{w}
"A... won... der~"{w}
note: Syllable-by-syllable fushigi with a music note: note -> '~' per convention; 'Won-der-ful' keeps the three beats. | accuracy: "Won-der-ful" turned the noun Bilente keeps demanding (fushigi = wonder) into praise; now the word itself, drawn out beat by beat. Editorial may restyle the beats. | editorial: three beats as in fu-shi-gi, the noun 'a wonder' Bilente keeps demanding (5152).

en: "Gyaaaaahhh!?{w}D-d-don't come near meeee!!"{w}
Beldoll went on a rampage!!{w}
note: Battle trigger line.

en: You sent Beldoll packing.{w}
note: Subject restored: the party.

en: "My apologies, everyone.{w}It seems this was nothing but an overhyped, disappointing toy."{w}
note: editorial: hyouban dake (overhyped) + katasukashi (disappointing) in Bilente's polite register; old line was clunky and slangy.

en: "D-dammit...{w}Hey, mister.{w}How do I become the ultimate wonder?"{w}
note: ossan = 'mister' (Beldoll's own word for Bilente).

en:
"That is something you must work out for yourself."{w}{p}"Well, since you're here,
why not take some inspiration from the items I've collected?{w}You'll find plenty of pieces much like yourself."{w}
"Hmm... Mister, you've sure collected all kinds of stuff.{w}I mean, this is awesome!"{w}{p}"Oh, even my senior's here!{w}Yo! Long time no see, sir!!"{w}
note: senpai = 'my senior' (the old-man statue, which the source calls an old man). 'sir' renders the -ssu deference. | editorial: word order: 'even' moved to read naturally.

en: Weird Old Statue
note: New name: kikai na roujin no chokoku, lit. 'bizarre statue of an old man'; shortened for the name box (16 chars).

en:
"What are you getting so worked up about, you blockhead!{w}Stop yapping for no reason!
How many times have I told you to build more atmosphere!!"{w}
"Gwoh... I'm frozen stiiiff!?"{w}
note: kanashibari: the statue's paralysis, which Bilente mentioned in slice_022 (row 5083).

en: "Honestly. It can't be helped.{w}I shall look after Beldoll here at the shop as well."{w}

"Since then, I've had Beldoll
help out with the housework
and learn all sorts of things."{w}{p}"The day Beldoll masters
a new act may not be far off."{w}{p}"When that day comes,
I would love for all of you to see it... Heh heh."{w}
note: editorial: Bilente's fufu = 'Heh heh' capitalised as in slice 022.

en: "Walmiiiiitt!!"{w}
note: Walmitt-san: elongated name; no Mr./Ms. (Walmitt's gender unknown).

en: Walmitt
"...Pipe down, Gregorio.{w}I won't lend you money, I won't give you money, and I don't have any to spare."{w}
"That's not iiit!{w}I came here to wooork!!"{w}
note: Gregorio's -zeeee tic rendered by stretching the last word.

en:
"Huh? You?{w}Good grief. Armitt did ask me about you,
but I never thought you'd actually show up."{w}{p}"What can you do? Any special skills?"{w}
note: Armitt = Gregorio's mother (washerwoman).

en: "I can do anythiiing!!"{w}

"Oh?{w}Then the shipyard has put out a call for shipwrights.
Want to give it a try?"{w}
"If I build 'em, they'll siiink!!"{w}
"That may well be true.{w}In that case... how about inventory management for a wholesaler?"{w}
"I'm no good at readin' and writiiing!!"{w}

"What? Then...
can you cook? I've got a request from a kitchen."{w}

"Food ain't for makin'!
It's for eatiiing!!"{w}

"Hmm... And you're not an adventurer either.
That means I have no work I can entrust to you right now."{w}
"Huh?"{w}

"Sorry. Profit comes first with me.{w}If my clients can't trust me, I can't make money."{w}{p}"If I sent a half-baked good-for-nothing like you out on a job,
the name Walmitt
would stop meaning anything as a brand."{w}{p}"Armitt asked me, I know,
but this is one thing I can't do anything about."{w}
"Aww, come ooon..."{w}

"If you want to work,
first learn a skill that's actually worth something out there.{w}Then come back."{w}
"Sniff, sniff..."{w}
note: uruuru = teary-eyed pleading look (Walmitt answers 'that look').

en: "Ah, no, no.{w}Looking at me like that won't work. Get lost.{w}Shoo! Shoo!!"{w}
"What a letdooown!{w}I ain't countin' on the likes of you ever agaaain!!"{w}{p}"Huh?{w}Walmitt, what's this request?{w}...Whoa, a 400,000 GP reward!?"{w}
"Ah, that request is void.{w}Do you know Heerdahl?"{w}

"Sure dooo!{w}My buddies say it's a grown-up playground
where you can get up to no goooood!!"{w}

"There's an arena there.{w}They want new fighters,
so the request asks us to send somebody."{w}

"Ooooh!
That's a great requeeest!{w}Rakin' in the caaash!!"{w}

note: kuro (black) = shady/criminal; 'dirty' keeps the one-word term Walmitt then asks about.

en: "Wha-huh!?"{w}
"...I'll do it."{w}
"Come again!?"{w}
note: editorial: aan!? is Walmitt's gruff 'huh?' (an? = 'Huh?' in 5249/5320); 'Excuse me' read as prim politeness.

en: "Meeee! I'm in, I'm in, I'm goin' iiin!!{w}I'm signin' uuup! Chaaampyooon!!"{w}
note: chanpyon = mangled 'champion', kept mangled.

en: "Don't be stupid! There's no telling what they'll do to you!!"{w}
"I'm super strooong!{w}Nobody can stand in my waaay!!"{w}
"No, no!{w}Give that request form back. I won't let you do it!!"{w}
"Nuh-uuuh!{w}I already took this jooob!!"{w}
"Stop that!{w}Hey, Gregorio!!"{w}
"Chaaampyooon!!"{w}
Gregorio left.{w}
"Ah... Don't blame me for this..."{w}
note: shiran zo watashi wa = 'I'm washing my hands of it'.

en:
"What's this? Who are you? Adventurers?"{w}{p}"I am Walmitt.{w}I serve as head of the merchants based in and around Port Saimar --
the Grand Merchant."{w}{p}"It's no exaggeration to say that nothing in the continent's trade
moves without passing through Saimar."{w}{p}"Because of that,
all sorts of troubles and requests for advice get brought to me."{w}{p}"Why don't you try handling
a few requests too, if you like?"{w}
note: Glossary: Grand Merchant, Port Saimar. | editorial: 'this Port Saimar' was unidiomatic. | proof: comma splice split ("What's this? Who are you?").

en:
"What, 'The Saimar Merchant's Companion'!?"{w}{p}"Where did you hear about it?{w}That booklet is supposed to be kept strictly secret
from anyone but merchants who trained in Saimar..."{w}{p}"What, some Costo at
the Kernel Shop in Bistel
wants it?"{w}{p}"Who is this Costo?{w}The only Costo
I can think of is the minister."{w}{p}"Besides, shouldn't Bistel's merchants
be trained by
Bistel's own merchants?"{w}{p}"If he insists,
send him to Saimar.{w}Once he's a full-fledged merchant, I'll give it to him."{w}{p}"Saimar is short on talent.{w}If he shows promise, I'll put him through
the wringer as Walmitt's successor."{w}
note: Booklet title reused from slice_011 row 3171. 'him' = the shop's Costo, the one who wants the booklet (yokoshitamae has no object; Costo is male per glossary). | editorial: 'top secret to anyone but' was unidiomatic.

en:
"...Huh?{w}Minister Costo wants it?{w}Hah! Nonsense."{w}{p}"Minister Costo would never make such a demand.{w}Why on earth would a minister
have to work an abacus?"{w}{p}"Besides, you're adventurers, aren't you?
Do you even know Minister Costo of the Administration Bureau?"{w}{p}"Minister Costo is the one who mediated so that trade among us in Saimar, Bistel,
Isfald and Semnadoc would run more smoothly, you know?"{w}{p}"If you so casually make false claims in the name of someone who's done so much,
I, Walmitt, won't stand for it, understand?"{w}
note: Daijin no Costo-dono / Gyoseikyoku no Costo-dono: both 'Minister Costo'. kimi is singular here but rendered 'you' for the party; 'adventurers' plural. | accuracy: kataru = to use a name falsely; draft "lightly using the name" lost the false claim, now "so casually make false claims in the name of".
Walmitt drops from kimitachi to the brusquer omaetachi here.
